text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix/KV cache hit-rate after the 2026-02-14 runtime roll (canary->prod). 92% -> ~67% on top-50 routes.
igor: who rolled what? any tokenizer changes or system-prompt tweaks in that deploy?
maya: deploy tag runtime-2026-02-14-v3. Main changes: kernel fallback selector (small perf tweak), batching heuristic tweak (max_batch_latency lowered), and we landed tokenizer update to tokenizers@1.0.0. Also a minor system prompt normalization change: we started injecting a truncated system note for some routes.
ryan: numbers from perf dashboard? which routes hit the most regression?
maya: copied sample from dashboards:
- route /chat/stream: hit-rate pre = 91.8% post = 66.9% (7d rolling)
- route /prompt/complete: pre = 93.4% post = 72.1%
- overall token cache hit-rate: 90.2% -> 70.8%
sam: that's huge. Could tokenizer changes shift tokenization of common prefixes, causing different cache keys? also system prompt injection will change prefix text -> different hashes.
igor: yes. Two orthogonal things: (1) tokenizer version bump changed BPE splits for emojis/whitespace sequences (we saw similar in staging earlier but small). (2) we changed canonicalization: used to trim trailing whitespace and canonicalize JSON fields in tool_call metadata; new change dropped canonicalization in some code paths for performance, meaning field ordering and insignificant whitespace now matter.
maya: re-played sample convo through old vs new tokenizer+canon on a top failing prefix; diff:
- old_norm: "system: You are Redwood Assistant\nuser: Summarize..."
- new_norm: "system: You are Redwood Assistant \nuser: Summarize..."  <-- extra space before newline
- tokenized_old: [101,234,55,...]
- tokenized_new: [101,234,56,...]  // mismatch at token index 3
ryan: even a single token difference causes cache miss. Our keying uses (model, tokenizer_version, raw_prefix_bytes, tool_meta_hash) right now, correct?
igor: key format: sha256(prefix_bytes || model || tokenizer_version || tool_meta_hash || seq_len_bucket). So tokenizer_version mismatch will avoid hit — intended. But if tokenizer stays same and only whitespace/ordering changes then hits should remain; except we removed canonicalization so raw_prefix_bytes diverge.
sam: what about function/tool_call fields? many clients started sending function call/metadata with extra ephemeral fields (trace_id, sdk_version). If those fields are in the prefix JSON and we don't strip them, keys diverge.
maya: we saw many requests with tool_meta like: {"tool":"db_fetch","sdk":"js-1.12","trace_id":"..."}
igor: proposed short-term mitigations:
- revert the canonicalization removal in hot path (re-enable stable JSON ordering and whitespace trim) — patch today
- for tokenizer bump: ensure tokenizer_version is part of cache key (it already is). For cross-version warmup, we need a migration plan.
ryan: long-term: we should make keying tolerant to non-semantic changes. Ideas:
- canonicalizer v2: stable JSON, remove known volatile fields (trace_id, request_id, sdk) via a whitelist/blacklist approach
- normalize whitespace/newlines: collapse multi-space, trim
- token-aware keying: compute key on token ids (fast path) rather than raw bytes to collapse tokenization differences — but that ties us to tokenizer CPU cost for key generation
- prefix clustering warmup: detect high-volume prefixes and pre-warm new variant caches when tokenizer_version changes
sam: token-aware keys sound robust but expensive. We could do hybrid: if prefix length < N tokens, do tokenization; else fallback to byte-hash. Or async tokenization: accept miss and enqueue warmup to populate cache for tokenized key.
igor: regarding warmup: we instrumented a warmup worker previously (warmup-v2) that can replay top N prefixes across model/tokenizer variants. We need to add tokenizer_version dimension and a dependency graph so when tokenizer bumps, we schedule warmups for delta.
maya: immediate steps I can take:
- roll forward patch to re-enable canonicalization in hot path (patch PR ready, CI green) — request approval
- add blacklist for known volatile tool fields (trace_id/sdk) in canonizer
- ramp warmup to include tokenizer_version
ryan: approvals: @igor please review the PR today. Also add a dashboard that shows cache-hit by tokenizer_version and by system_prompt version so we can see drift.
igor: ack, reviewing now. Also let's add a small experiment: change cache key to include normalized 'system_prompt_hash' instead of full system prompt bytes to allow controlled rollout of system prompt tweaks.
sam: quick note on batching heuristics: lowering max_batch_latency reduced batch sizes slightly which increases per-token work and might slightly change request interleaving, but shouldn't affect prefix identity. Keep in mind for next time to separate infra/perf changes from semantic changes in same deploy.
infra-bot: deploy runtime-2026-02-14-v3 recorded: kernel-selector-optimizations, batching-latency-tweak, tokenizers@1.0.0
maya: ok action items: (1) revert canonicalization removal (patch -> deploy), (2) blacklist volatile fields, (3) schedule warmup job for top 1k prefixes across tokenizer versions, (4) add dashboard by tokenizer/system_prompt. I'll follow up with timelines.
ryan: +1. add follow-up thread for rollout plan once we confirm hotfix impact. :eyes:
